headline: Data Center Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, primarily data centers, pay for the costs of new grid infrastructure required by their operations, preventing these costs from being passed to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Governor Abigail Spanberger, environmental groups, State Corporation Commission (SCC).
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users, business advocacy groups.
news_headline: Virginia requires data centers to pay for their own power lines
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission decided that data centers must pay the full cost for transmission infrastructure projects they require, preventing these billions of dollars in costs from falling on residential ratepayers. Governor Abigail Spanberger supported this move, which is expected to save Virginia residents hundreds of millions of dollars.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates increased reporting requirements for data centers regarding their water consumption, providing transparency for water management and future policy decisions.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, local communities, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: Data centers are drinking more water, but overall water use in Virginia has gone down anyway. Here are the numbers.
news_summary: While overall water use in Virginia has decreased, data centers' water consumption has significantly increased, with a single large data center potentially using millions of gallons daily. SB 553 aims to bring transparency to this issue by requiring data centers to report their water usage, which is a concern for environmental advocates and local communities.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for sound profiles near residential areas and schools, and allowing localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Delegate Joshua Thomas.
opponents: Data center industry, real estate developers, business advocacy groups.
news_headline: Virginia's 'Data Center Alley' residents say an eerie hum is keeping them up at night
news_summary: Residents in Loudoun County, Virginia, are experiencing constant noise from nearby data centers, described as an 'eerie hum' that affects their well-being and sleep. HB 153 addresses these concerns by requiring site assessments for sound profiles and allowing localities to consider other environmental impacts before approving new data center developments.
